dimensions.description: Actual time before a useful or mandatory decision, plus time available for preparation, participation and follow-through. A deadline is a constraint, not proof of authority.
Plausible downside for this bounded action if wrong. Use the most consequential credible affected group and explain the basis; do not average harms.

values.label: Minor
values.anchor: Small local inconvenience; no material obligation or protection affected.

values.label: Meaningful local
values.anchor: Rework, missed local commitment or limited cost to an identifiable group; ordinary recovery is feasible.

values.label: Material
values.anchor: Substantial resources, multiple teams, important external commitments or lasting relationship consequences; explicit owner review matters.

values.label: Severe or protected
values.anchor: Credible safety, rights, livelihood, major irreversible loss or regulated consequence; appropriate qualified process and protections govern.

dimensions.description: Ability to stop and restore the proposed change, including downstream and human consequences. A nominal rollback is not evidence that all harms can be undone.

values.label: Irreversible
values.anchor: A meaningful consequence cannot be restored within an acceptable boundary.

values.label: Partial or costly
values.anchor: Some consequences can be undone, but important residue, delay or cost remains.

values.label: Recoverable
values.anchor: A credible named recovery route can restore the relevant boundary with an accepted cost/time; verify it before a live test.

values.label: Easy and verified
values.anchor: A small bounded action can be stopped promptly and restoration has been checked for the relevant scope, without unacceptable residual harm.

dimensions.description: How the response could become knowable. Different subproblems can have different states; this is not a mandatory Cynefin classification.

values.label: Established response
values.anchor: Relevant procedure or demonstrated know-how exists and applies to this task.

values.label: Analysis required
values.anchor: A qualified examination can evaluate the options or determine missing technical facts.

values.label: Learning through bounded action
values.anchor: Interactions or adaptation make the response context-dependent, with a specific reason beyond missing information; only an authorised safe bounded test may answer it.

values.label: Mixed
values.anchor: Different parts require different knowledge approaches; separate them before selecting a method.

dimensions.description: What kind of disagreement or shared purpose is evidenced. Multiple causes may coexist; do not infer hidden motives.

values.label: Shared intended result
values.anchor: Relevant people explicitly agree on the desired result; implementation can still differ.

values.label: Outcome or criteria unclear
values.anchor: No adequately specified or shared result/criterion has been established.

values.label: Competing legitimate interests
values.anchor: Parties state different priorities, costs or needs despite understanding the facts.

values.label: Facts or causal account disputed
values.anchor: People disagree about observations, assumptions or explanations.

values.label: Mixed disagreement
values.anchor: Both purpose/interests and accounts are disputed; separate them rather than assume a single cause.

values.label: Conflicting priorities
values.anchor: A broad aim may be shared but competing sequencing, deadlines or resource claims are stated.

values.label: Goal disputed
values.anchor: Relevant people do not agree that the intended result should be pursued.

dimensions.description: Where dependencies relevant to the action lie. Record actual owners and dependencies alongside the category; size does not measure difficulty.

values.label: Individual
values.anchor: The immediate preparation/action has no required joint decision.

values.label: Two-party
values.anchor: Two people must coordinate or reach a bounded understanding.

values.label: Within one team
values.anchor: Several people work within a clear local decision boundary.

values.label: Across owners
values.anchor: Separate teams, functions or parties control required inputs or decisions.

values.label: Multiple interacting boundaries
values.anchor: Several dependencies/decision centres must be mapped; no single local owner controls the full result.

dimensions.description: Observed missing support for the particular task. Select only evidenced gaps; 'none' requires an affirmative account and cannot coexist with another selection.

values.label: No demonstrated gap
values.anchor: Relevant participants report and evidence adequate support for the bounded task.

values.label: Task skill or knowledge
values.anchor: A relevant observed attempt or explained experience indicates instruction/practice is needed.

values.label: Available effort
values.anchor: Work demand exceeds stated time/energy allocation; do not infer laziness.

values.label: Expectations or authority boundary
values.anchor: The result, quality threshold, ownership or retained decisions are not understood.

values.label: Tools, access to expertise or materials
values.anchor: Required practical support is missing despite skill and willingness.

values.label: Participation access
values.anchor: Format, schedule, language or access arrangements impede participation; ask preferences without requiring diagnosis.

values.label: Relevant information
values.anchor: Necessary task information is unavailable or unreliable.

values.label: Authority boundary
values.anchor: The proposed decision is outside the user's known remit or the owner is unresolved; treat as a gate, never a compensable fit preference.

values.label: Priority clarity
values.anchor: Conflicting assignments lack an authorised ordering or tradeoff.

dimensions.description: Whether the proposed interaction allows meaningful participation and dissent. This is a contextual account, never a psychological-safety scale or proof of confidentiality.

values.label: No specific barrier reported
values.anchor: Current accounts identify no particular obstacle to this format. This is not proof of safety or an independent assessment; the manager's silence is not employee agreement.

values.label: Power or access constraints
values.anchor: Hierarchy, dependency, format or pressure could inhibit contribution; adapt or use a safer channel.

values.label: Credible protection concern
values.anchor: Reported coercion, retaliation or serious harm makes the proposed joint interaction inappropriate pending a suitable protection/independent process.
